overview: A strong storm is crossing the West this week, with snow for the Sierra and Wasatch now and a brief lull Friday night. Several weaker systems follow over the weekend and into the Thanksgiving week, with the Cascades seeing more snow Sunday.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A strong storm is moving across the Sierra with heavy mountain snow through Thursday night, and a Winter Storm Warning runs above 4000 feet until 4 AM Friday. Kirkwood has the biggest total so far at 17 inches. The NWS is calling for 23 to 39 inches Thursday night through Sunday night. Expect drier weather Friday afternoon, then frost Saturday morning.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: A potent storm is bringing heavy snow to the Sierra with strong winds and hazardous travel through Friday morning. Mammoth has 14 inches so far, and the NWS is calling for 21 to 32 inches Thursday night through Thursday night. A brief dry spell follows Friday afternoon, then another system arrives Saturday afternoon.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A closed low is sending snow east, with the heaviest totals on higher ground through Friday. Grand Targhee leads at 12 inches, and the NWS is calling for 12 to 25 inches Thursday night through Monday. Snow showers continue through the weekend into early next week, with cooler temperatures.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A longer storm arrives in pieces from Thursday morning through Saturday morning, with the highest totals in the northern mountains. Powder Mountain has 11 inches, and the NWS is calling for 19 to 35 inches Thursday through Monday. A Winter Weather Advisory runs Thursday through Saturday. Valley snow is possible Friday evening into Saturday morning.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A low off Oregon is spreading rain and mountain snow today, with the upper low moving into California and the Great Basin through Friday. Dry weather returns briefly Friday afternoon. Another system arrives Saturday, with Crystal Mountain getting the most snow on Sunday at 6 inches.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a trough will bring additional West Coast rain and mountain snow around Thursday Nov 26, with a possible heavier rain event for California Tuesday Nov 24 into Wednesday Nov 25.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
